# HISTORY: the `mjc` node — a big-picture arc

*Auto-generated qualitative history. Overwrite freely; see [README.md](README.md) / [FILES.md](FILES.md) for the standing technical summary this complements.*

## Why this substrate exists

Born 2026-07-16 from [`ideas/physical_control_substrate.md`](../../ideas/physical_control_substrate.md), prompted by asking where a "vanilla" scaling+imitation robot policy is *structurally* confounded. The founding fork, stated on day one and never relitigated since: MuJoCo as a **controllable-dynamics DGP** (knobs you set and sweep, a vanilla baseline, a slope/dissociation as the deliverable) — never an RL-to-SOTA robotics benchmark. It was pitched as the missing rung between RHM (discrete, known latents) and language (continuous, opaque): real contact and a real command channel, without giving up the ability to *intervene on the generator*, which RHM's whole value rests on. A secondary, more speculative motivation — biology as a source of hypotheses (efference copy, cerebellar recalibration) tested on an actual body — turned out to be the thread that mattered most; the "credibility with reviewers" motivation barely resurfaces.

The repo's own git history for this path starts abruptly at a 2026-07-22 "mjc reorg" commit (this monorepo consolidates several prior projects), but the internal document dates recover the real timeline from 2026-07-16 onward. Read chronologically, the node's prose is unusually self-aware about its own reasoning — README's routinely narrate *why* a result changed the plan, not just what the result was. That self-narration is mined below.

## Act I — Establishing the substrate is real physics, not a toy (Cuts #1–#3, 07-16 → 07-18)

[`contact_residual/`](contact_residual/README.md) ported the a2a "residual reflects surprise" idea onto contact and found something sharper than expected: the FM residual is an **event detector**, spiking at the free→contact transition and decaying within ~4 steps even while contact *persists* for 20+. Two small retractions already appear here — plain MSE was dropped for Huber once contact's heavy tail was found to swamp free-flight learning, and a "residual rank ∝ DGP complexity" hypothesis (carried in from MNIST/RHM) was explicitly abandoned when eff-rank went the *wrong* direction.

[`arity_torque/`](arity_torque/README.md) then closed RHM's long-standing "received-wisdom" confound by forcing i.i.d. commands, and got the cleanest version yet of the arity claim: the smallest command-aware model beat the largest command-blind one, at every capacity. No retraction — the note here is that physics gave the team a *more legible instrument* than the glimpse/region-edit constructions arity had relied on before.

[`dynamics_shift/`](dynamics_shift/README.md) is where the substrate earned its keep: the one move only a controllable-dynamics DGP enables is intervening on the *transition operator* while holding the task fixed. The first framing — a static "degradation slope," lifted from the a2a OOD-robustness playbook — was explicitly retired as "theoretically shaky" and replaced with a cleaner one: reward-free re-adaptation. A per-step-replanning pilot came back near-null (feedback substitutes for a correct model), which forced the `replan_every` open-loop-commit design that became the arc's recurring instrument. The closing biological reading here — ballistic movement / cerebellar recalibration vs. basal-ganglia reward-driven relearning — is named in-doc as **the seed of the entire ballistic arc** that would only land seven nodes later.

## Act II — The first real pivot: from mechanism-first to phenomenon-first (07-18)

[`value_shaping/`](value_shaping/README.md) was built as the deliberately **stationary control** the two-timescale program would need before any outer loop could claim credit for something beyond it. Its most useful content is a graveyard of failed substrate designs (a heavy puck failed because "energy ≠ prediction cost"; contact itself turned out irreducible and had to be designed around) — and a fragile-effect downgrade: the hoped-for capacity-efficiency "teeth" appeared at low data and vanished at scale, demoted from headline to caveat.

[`directed_readapt/`](directed_readapt/README.md) delivered two clean negatives — a global shift has no scarcity to exploit; a localized patch has scarcity, but disagreement-driven exploration is **blind to confident-wrongness**, under-visiting exactly the region a dynamics shift corrupts. This is also where a previously-treated-as-universal ranking (disagreement beats surprise) is explicitly retracted into "which drive wins is set by the regime, not absolute." And it's where the node's most explicit pivot language appears, dated 2026-07-18: an end to "a chapter of a-priori mechanistic-atom verification" in favor of going **phenomenon-first** — build the actual compounding-adaptation effect across a drift sequence first, then back-translate mechanism from what works. Everything from here through `drift_value_loop/` executes that program.

## Act III — The meta-learning arc: cuts #4 → #4e ([`meta_adapt/`](meta_adapt/README.md))

Framed against RHM's meta-learning collapse, this arc treated the meta−multitask gap as an *order parameter* rather than a checkbox and found the bifurcation directly: a 1-D damping family collapses to zero gap (the RHM floor, reproduced); an actuator-rotation family with input-coupled conflict opens the gap monotonically. #4b then split a thing the team had assumed was one phenomenon into two: a context latent decodes the task parameter equally well in both regimes but only *pays off* under conflict — "true but useless" at the floor. #4c delivered a clean negative on value-of-information collection (naive max-magnitude beats VoI when the informative action is just the biggest one — VoI is over-engineering for 1-D system-ID). #4d hit a load-bearing false start (position-only value-matching "collapsed to a vacuous loss") before landing on full-support matching, and only then found value-shaping buys control when capacity is genuinely binding — not always. #4e closed the causal loop with a reward-driven outer loop, but only after diagnosing a concrete wireheading instance (a scale/grad-clip confound) and fixing it with "read the CEM's converged distribution, not its single best candidate."

## Act IV — Curiosity as the afferent complement ([`curiosity_control/`](curiosity_control/README.md))

Supplies the "where to look" half to #4d/#4e's "what to keep" half. The clean confirmation (a reducible-surprise drive tracks a moving frontier, and the benefit is specifically non-stationary) is overshadowed by a genuine surprise: on this substrate, disagreement-based curiosity **falls for the noisy TV** — a direct inversion of the earlier active-vision result, because low-dimensional aleatoric noise makes ensemble members disagree rather than converge. The fix that emerged wasn't a smarter reducibility filter but **grounding**: adding the exploit/value signal as a second additive drive rather than a hard gate, immunizing against the noisy TV and producing an interior optimum — described in-doc as "the explore-exploit framing of meta-learning made behavioral."

## Act V — The keystone attempt, and an obstruction reinterpreted as confirmation ([`online_value_loop/`](online_value_loop/README.md))

This is the node's most important reframing moment. The idea doc's named keystone — a single, fully-online two-timescale loop — was built both ways (afferent and efferent) and **obstructed on both levers**: CEM-MPC control turned out robust to the curiosity drive's tracking effect, and value-shaping's benefit is a slow, commit-dependent, pre-convergence *transient* invisible to a live local reward gradient. Rather than read this as a project-level failure, the doc reframes it explicitly: the obstruction is "a positive confirmation that value must live on the slow timescale" — i.e., the failure to build the fast loop is evidence *for* the two-timescale premise, not against it. This licenses the arc's second big reframe: value's benefit is an **adaptation-speed** effect, not a converged-competence effect — which only makes sense in a world that never converges, i.e., under perpetual drift. That's the next experiment, by name.

## Act VI — Executing that named experiment ([`drift_value_loop/`](drift_value_loop/README.md))

Compounding across a drift sequence is real, but the source is reassigned: it comes from the **memory architecture** (a context-latent climbs 0.31→0.97 across shifts; pooled monolithic memory actively *anti-compounds* under conflict), not from value-carving, which turns out capacity-gated and control-robust — a clean null, echoing #4c/#4d. The pivotal diagnostic here is that control is "a near-blind grader" of value — a replanning controller reaches goals about as well with a stale model as a fresh one, so grading the self-tuner on control makes it wander. Re-grading on **value-relevant FM prediction error** (the literal cerebellum→VTA signal) instead of reward gives the explore/exploit balance a clean interior optimum where control was flat. Stated plainly in-doc: "the missing piece was never the value structure — it was the teacher."

## Act VII — Ballistic control: the missing variable was the control mode ([`ballistic/`](ballistic/README.md))

Directly attacks `drift_value_loop`'s stubborn negative (replanning as a blind grader) by asking whether that's a fact about value or about **control mode**. A feedforward/committed controller makes FM quality ~3× more behaviorally load-bearing and reward-free re-adaptation ~4.3× more restorative than reactive control — closing the "efferent bridge" the founding idea doc had flagged as missing seven nodes earlier. Cut 4a's first attempt to derive this from the value loop's own endogenous drive failed for an instructive reason: "the intended explore/exploit roles invert" in the test geometry — a confound, not a null — forcing abandonment of the endogenous drive for a manufactured axis (4b) and explicitly deferring "directed collection" to a child node, [`ballistic/directed/`](ballistic/directed/README.md).

## Act VIII — The embodiment audit: teleportation was a standing unrealism ([`on_policy/`](on_policy/README.md), [`COLLECTION_REALISM.md`](on_policy/COLLECTION_REALISM.md))

The memo that opens this line is itself a retraction document: it audits the entire prior tree and finds every experiment had been running on free, omniscient teleportation, making every absolute sample-count claim an unlabeled upper bound, and making `ballistic/directed/`'s S2 directed-collection result **unmeasurable** — a 22× "measurement subsidy" that had silently demoted relevance to a tiebreaker. `on_policy/` built the fix as a flag (teleport bit-identical, gated, kept as the code default; on-policy adopted as the *convention* for new cuts) and then delivered three self-correcting findings in a row: **E0** found on-policy's apparent edge was mostly a mistuned teleport default, not embodiment; **E1** *refuted the memo's own hypothesis*, backwards — a globally-learnable drift re-adapts equally well from any motion; **E2** finally located where embodiment costs something (local drift, 2.5× more transitions, because data gathered under a wrong model is itself wrong-distributed) and retired the memo's guessed mechanism ("coverage grows") for a sharper one. **E3** ([`directed_on_policy/`](on_policy/directed_on_policy/README.md)) then reran the retracted S2 claim once looking was embodied and metered, and it came back positive (1.84× subsidy, not 22×) — "the retracted claim is now measurable and positive."

## Act IX — Expansion: the founding idea doc retracts its own flagship claim ([`expansion/`](expansion/README.md))

The idea doc's most ambitious pitch — "drifting dynamics is a novelty generator," which should make a forward model expand its representable directions — is directly tested here and the idea doc itself now carries the retraction inline: *"⚠️ Retired 2026-07-27 ... It does not."* The measured null (±0.08 directions) is calibrated against a known-real effect (+0.72 ± 0.42 from genuine DOF accretion), so the null has a scale rather than being silence — built as **calibrate → measure → calibrate** specifically because three earlier rank-based instruments in this repo had failed from unrelated saturation, and "a null read off a fourth such instrument would have been worth nothing." The reframe that survives: *drift moves the target function; expansion grows the space of representable functions* — a fixed-DOF motor plant has no hierarchy to expand into, and the belief's real claim needs re-testing in a domain that has one ([`rhm/residual_decomposition/`](../rhm/residual_decomposition/README.md)).

## Act X — A second task family, built to retire a caveat ([`arm_substrate/`](arm_substrate/README.md))

Purpose-built to remove ballistic's "single-family" caveat. Its own README contains an explicit "corrections to the substrate's own pitch" section: capacity does *not* bind on the natural first choice (a 2-link arm), only at n≥5, and kinematic redundancy does **not** give the droppable subspace the design had assumed. Once corrected, it validated the ballistic thesis transfers (5.24× vs. the pusher's 4.3×) and produced a mirror-signed aftereffect the pusher's geometry structurally could not.

## Act XI — The live thread: cross-pollinating with RHM ([`on_policy/metered_repair/`](on_policy/metered_repair/README.md), 07-29 → 07-31)

The most recent work explicitly ports two claims from [`rhm/directed_sculpting/full_loop/`](../rhm/directed_sculpting/full_loop/README.md) onto the arm and checks which survive the substrate change. **E4**: RHM's diagnosis that a fixed-budget counterfactual tap measures data-starvation rather than reducibility **ports exactly** (inverted here too), and the repaired tap reallocates far better by every process measure — but the repair **does not cash out** in outcome (control-neutral, 1/3 seeds), even as `value` matches a privileged oracle on an inverted tap. The one clean positive is a conjunction result made askable only by this substrate's geometry: with a visited-but-irreducible cell placed, relevance alone becomes the *worst* arm, and reducibility rescues it — closing a mirror-image degeneracy neither substrate could see alone (RHM has no visited-irreducible cell; mjc had no visited-irrelevant one, until now). **E5** returns a clean negative with a mechanical diagnosis: a fixed-DOF plant with spatially-gated fields gives an MLP no route to shared-parameter inference, so repair does not migrate between regions with identical drift — extending Act IX's conclusion from the expansion question to the necessity question. Section 4 closes with an unresolved diagnostic (outcome is not a monotone function of any allocation-process column measured) flagged as the thing to explain before trusting any allocation tap further.

## The shape of the whole arc

Read end to end, the node's central discipline is **retraction as a load-bearing move, not a failure mode**: nearly every major node opens by naming what the previous node got wrong or measured under a hidden subsidy (teleportation, a mistuned drive, a confounded geometry, a founding idea doc's own hypothesis), and treats the correction as the result. The two biggest reframes — value is a *slow, committed* quantity rather than a fast online one, and the missing ingredient in directed collection was *the teacher* (what grades the loop), not *the structure* (what the loop contains) — both came from obstructions the team chose to interpret rather than route around. The substrate's own realism was itself put on trial (teleport → embodied collection) and found selectively, not uniformly, unrealistic (free under global drift, expensive under local drift) — which is the same shape of finding as the arity and expansion results: **the substrate's affordances are not uniform, and the node's job is to locate exactly where they break**, not to assume either that physics helps everywhere or that it helps nowhere.

## Where it stands now

The live open threads, per [`README.md`](README.md)'s "Next steps": re-attempting the retracted S2 directed-collection question on the local-drift on-policy substrate (metering probes to the same budget the loop pays); testing whether ensemble disagreement's job is recoverable now that on-policy creates genuinely unvisited territory; and explaining `metered_repair` E4's unpredicted outcome column before trusting any allocation tap further. The dimensionality-expansion belief's actual core claim — does novelty grow representable directions — remains untested everywhere, and the node's own conclusion is that it does not belong on a motor plant at all.
